profile.name: Sony Group Corporation
profile.summary: Sony Group Corporation develops, designs, produces, manufactures, supplies, and sells electronic equipment, instruments, and devices for consumer, professional, and industrial use in Japan, the United States, Europe, China, the Asia-Pacific, and internationally. The company operates through Game & Network Services, Music, Pictures, Entertainment Technology & Services, and Imaging & Sensing Solutions. It develops, designs, produces, manufactures, provides, and sells smartphones and image sensors; plans, produces, manufactures, and sells music software, performances and merchandise, song lyrics and music management, licensing, animation works, and game applications. The company is also involved in the production, acquisition, sale, and distribution of motion pictures and television programs; operates television networks and direct-to-consumer distribution services; insurance business, including life insurance and non-life insurance; internet banking; production and sale of digital software add-on content; manufacturing and sales of home video game consoles; and interchangeable lens, projectors, and medical equipment. It has a strategic partnership with TCL Electronics Holdings Limited in the home entertainment sector; and a non-binding memorandum of understanding with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited for a strategic partnership regarding the development and manufacturing of image sensors. The company was formerly known as Sony Corporation and changed its name to Sony Group Corporation in April 2021. Sony Group Corporation was incorporated in 1946 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

trends.claim: The global games market is forecast to grow 6.1% to $213.9 billion in 2026, with player and spender growth.
trends.why: Higher industry spending lifts Sony's PlayStation software, services, and subscription revenue.
trends.quote: The global games market is forecast to generate $213.9 billion in 2026, an increase of 6.1% year over year.
trends.impact_basis: G&NS is a major revenue stream
trends.theme_definition: Worldwide consumer spending on video games expands across platforms and regions.

trends.claim: The PC and console market is no longer the growth engine it once was, with players more selective in 2026.
trends.why: Slower PC/console growth pressures Sony's console hardware and game software revenue.
trends.quote: The PC and console market is not in decline, but it is no longer the growth engine it once was.
trends.theme_definition: PC and console gaming growth slows as hardware cycles stretch and players become more selective.

trends.claim: Physical video game dollar sales fell to an all-time July low of $85 million in the US in 2026.
trends.why: Sony's disc exit cuts manufacturing costs but risks retail backlash and physical revenue.
trends.quote: physical software dollar sales plunged to an all-time July low of $85 million in the US
trends.impact_basis: Physical is a minority of G&NS revenue
trends.theme_definition: Consumer purchases of boxed video games shrink as digital distribution takes over.

trends.claim: Global recorded music revenues grew 6.4% to $31.7 billion in 2025, with paid streaming up 8.8%.
trends.why: Higher streaming and subscription revenue lifts Sony Music's recorded music income.
trends.quote: Global recorded music revenues grew 6.4% and reached US$31.7 billion in 2025
trends.impact_basis: Music is a major Sony revenue stream
trends.theme_definition: Paid streaming subscriptions drive global recorded music revenue growth.

trends.claim: Global recorded music retail revenues are forecast to grow 62.9% from $74.3 billion in 2025 to $121.1 billion by 2033, led by expanded rights.
trends.why: Expanded rights and fan economy add higher-margin revenue for Sony Music.
trends.quote: Global recorded music retail revenues will grow by 62.9%, from $74.3 billion in 2025 to $121.1 billion by 2033
trends.theme_definition: Labels diversify beyond streaming into merchandise, live, and expanded rights.

trends.claim: Global consumer tech sales are projected to be flat in 2026, at -0.4% year over year, after 3% growth in 2025.
trends.why: Flat consumer electronics demand pressures Sony's TV, audio, and camera sales.
trends.quote: For 2026, the global picture will flatten, with NIQ estimating -0.4% year-over-year growth.
trends.impact_basis: Entertainment Technology & Services is a major stream
trends.theme_definition: Global consumer technology spending stalls after prior growth, with regional divergence.

trends.claim: The global consumer electronics market is estimated to grow to $740 billion in 2026, a 7% CAGR through 2036.
trends.why: Expanding consumer electronics market supports Sony's TV, audio, and camera revenue.
trends.quote: demand for consumer electronics is estimated to grow to USD 740 billion in 2026
trends.impact_basis: Entertainment Technology & Services is a major stream
trends.theme_definition: Worldwide consumer electronics spending expands on replacement cycles and premium adoption.

trends.claim: Memory chip prices doubled in Q1 2026 and are forecast to rise up to 63% in Q2 due to AI data centre demand.
trends.why: Higher memory costs raise PlayStation console production costs and may force price increases.
trends.quote: Memory chip prices doubled in the first quarter alone from the previous quarter and are forecast to climb up to 63% in the current quarter
trends.size_basis: no market size; memory prices doubled, +63% forecast
trends.theme_definition: AI-driven demand tightens supply of memory and other electronic components, raising costs.

trends.claim: China's share of US console imports fell from 86% in 2024 to under 5% in 2025, with Vietnam capturing 75%.
trends.why: Tariff avoidance lowers landed costs but relocation and Vietnam tariffs add expense.
trends.quote: China’s share of US console imports dropped from 86% in 2024 to less than 5% in 2025. Vietnam captured 75% of the market.
trends.theme_definition: Tariffs push console and electronics production from China to Vietnam and other locations.

trends.claim: Global foundry revenues are projected to reach $218.8 billion in 2026, up 24.8%, with TSMC 5nm/4nm capacity fully booked and prices raised.
trends.why: Tight foundry capacity and higher wafer prices raise Sony's chip procurement costs.
trends.quote: TSMC’s 5nm/4nm and below capacity could be fully booked for the remainder of 2026. In addition, TSMC has raised its prices at 5nm/4nm and below.
trends.impact_basis: G&NS chip costs, material but not total
trends.theme_label: Foundry capacity tightness and price hikes
trends.theme_definition: AI demand fills leading-edge foundry capacity, raising wafer prices for chip buyers.

trends.claim: In FY2025, contracts won by sales staff at nine major Japanese life insurers rose 25% year over year, overtaking bank channels.
trends.why: Sony Life's face-to-face sales force benefits as customers seek support.
trends.quote: 2025年度は主要生保9社の営業職員が獲得した契約保険料が前の年度比25%増えた。銀行などの金融機関の窓口経由の保険料を逆転した。
trends.impact_basis: Financial Services stream, life insurance distribution
trends.theme_definition: Japanese life insurers see face-to-face sales regain share from bank channels.

trends.claim: In an undated 2026 report, brand-owned D2C channels are expanding at 9.92% CAGR, while traditional offline distribution grows at 3.42%.
trends.why: Direct sales improve margin but require channel investment and disrupt retail partners.
trends.quote: Brand-owned D2C channels are expanding at 9.92% CAGR, while traditional offline distribution moves at 3.42%.
trends.theme_definition: Consumer electronics brands increasingly sell direct to consumers, bypassing traditional distribution.
